text:
Harish Reddy: collecting operator pain points on the new provisioning CLI while it’s fresh. please reply w/ what tripped you up + “small fix” vs “needs workstream”.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1. we can knock out small UX stuff this week. keep it concrete: command you ran, what you expected, what happened.

Harish Reddy: my list from yesterday’s staging expansion:
- `rw-provision run` prints “successfully started” but doesn’t print the run id unless you add `-v` (i had to go to console -> search pool id)
- error output on failure is too terse. saw `VALIDATION_FAILED` w/ no hint which gate. expected “gpu-health: ECC errors on node i-0abc…” or “dns: cannot resolve …”
- `--dry-run` is confusing: it still hits control plane and creates a run record. i expected “plan only / no mutation”.

Gabe Wilson: on run id: agreed, that’s a bug/oversight. should always print run_id + link. easy.

Kira Thompson: can we also print the “next action” in failures? like “rerun `rw-provision stage rerun --stage validating` after fixing helm values” vs just failing.

Victor Alvarez: networking checks output is rough:
- it just says “TLS check failed”
- doesn’t tell you WHICH endpoint/cert it tested
- no command to reproduce locally
would love something like:
`tls: failed to connect to https://<pool>.svc.<region>.redwood.ai:443 (x509: unknown authority)`

Harish Reddy: +1. also, the help text on regions:
`--region` accepts `us-east-1` but the docs/examples use `iad`/`sfo` sometimes. i typed `iad` out of habit and got “invalid region” w/ no mapping.

Nina Petrova: that’s because internal naming vs cloud region. CLI should accept aliases OR print “did you mean us-east-1?”

Keiko Yamamoto: another one: stage names.
`rw-provision stage rerun --stage bootstrap` -> says invalid stage; actual stage is `bootstrapping`.
maybe allow prefixes/aliases? or `--stage bootstrapping` should be discoverable via `rw-provision stages`.

Gabe Wilson: we have the canonical enum in control plane, but we can add friendly aliases in CLI layer. + add `rw-provision run describe <run_id>` that lists stages + current.

Jamal Pierce: metrics side: would be great if CLI prints correlation id in a copy/paste-friendly way.
right now it logs `correlation_id=...` but mixed with other text. can we do:
`Correlation ID: p2r_01H...` on its own line.

Sahana Iyer: small one: CLI requires you to pass `--config` path even when you’re just querying status. maybe split commands:
- `rw-provision run start --config ...`
- `rw-provision run status --run-id ...`

Rafael Mendes: + for SRE: exit codes matter.
- currently both “invalid args” and “stage failed” exit 1
- we want distinct codes so automation can decide “retry vs user fix”.

Harish Reddy: another gotcha: `rw-provision run status` defaults to printing last 50 events but it’s newest-first. makes it hard to see progression. can default to chronological, and add `--tail` if you want newest.

Vanessa Ortiz: keep them coming. i’m turning these into follow-ups.

Gabe Wilson: also saw confusing output in `--watch` mode (or what we’re calling watch): it refreshes but doesn’t show which stage is active, just “state=Provisioning”. we should show both:
`state=Bootstrapping (stage=bootstrap_helm)`

Kira Thompson: and please print the runbook link right in the error.
we have the runbooks now; something like:
`See: https://confluence.redwood.ai/.../dedicated-pool-provisioning-runbook#Bootstrapping`

Victor Alvarez: + include “how to re-run just networking checks” if that’s supported. people keep re-running entire pipeline when it’s just DNS.

Gabe Wilson: rerun-per-stage is supported for validating (and some bootstrap) but not all gates yet. we should be explicit: if not supported, print “stage rerun not available for <stage>; rerun from <previous checkpoint>”.

Harish Reddy: re: `--dry-run` expectation. if we can’t make it totally non-mutating, maybe rename it?
- `--preview` (no infra changes, but creates run record)
or
- `--dry-run` truly no run record, just validates config locally (schema + policy)

Benji Okafor: (jumping in from platform) we already have local schema validation in the library. CLI can do a “local validate” without calling the API. +1 to making that the default dry-run.

Vanessa Ortiz: ok, capturing as:
1) change `--dry-run` to “local validate only”
2) new flag `--preview` for “create run record but don’t execute stages” (if we still want that)

Gabe Wilson: i’ll file issues now. will reply w/ links.

redwood-bot: Vanessa Ortiz added a reaction :eyes: to Harish Reddy’s message

Gabe Wilson: created follow-ups:
- ENG-2761 “CLI: always print run_id + console link + correlation id”
- ENG-2762 “CLI: stage aliases + `rw-provision stages` + better help output”
- ENG-2763 “CLI: improve failure surface area (gate name, reason, next action, runbook links)”
- ENG-2764 “CLI: dry-run semantics (local validate) + rename preview”
- ENG-2765 “CLI: exit codes for args vs transient vs terminal failure”

Harish Reddy: :thumbsup: thank you. one more: when you pass a bad pool id, error is “404” but no hint if it’s “doesn’t exist” vs “no permission”. can CLI differentiate and say “check you’re on prod/staging env”?

Rafael Mendes: yes please. we keep burning time on “wrong environment” (staging vs prod) esp during pilots. maybe make CLI prompt if you try to run against prod without `--confirm-prod`.

Vanessa Ortiz: careful: prompts break automation. but we can require `--env prod` explicitly for mutating commands, and default to staging.

Sahana Iyer: + add `RW_ENV=prod` env var support. right now some folks assumed it reads kube context.

Gabe Wilson: ack. environment selection is messy today. i’ll append to ENG-2761 or make separate.

Keiko Yamamoto: also minor: output includes ANSI color codes even when piping to file. can detect non-tty and disable, or add `--no-color`.

Kira Thompson: and `--json` output option for status so we can attach to tickets / post to slack. right now it’s pretty but not machine readable.

Jamal Pierce: +1 `--json` esp if we want to backfill stage timings from operator-triggered runs.

Gabe Wilson: added:
- ENG-2766 “CLI: --json output + --no-color + tty detection”

Harish Reddy: thanks. for immediate small fix: can we at least print the run id on start today? that one’s the biggest papercut.

Gabe Wilson: yes. i can do a small PR today and get it into the next build.

Vanessa Ortiz: amazing. once PR is up, drop link here and we’ll ping Connor for the release train.

Gabe Wilson: will do.
